Things a man learns
after his first real failure
Failure is an event, not your identity. A business that closed or an exam you failed doesn't define who you are.
Your real friends show themselves. The people who call after a failure are the ones worth keeping close for life.
You can survive more than you thought. The fear of failing was often worse than the failure itself. Remember that next time.
Every failure has a lesson. Write down what went wrong and what you'd change. That list is worth a fortune later.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. History is full of great men who failed many times first.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. History is full of great men who failed many times first.

slides.texte_overlay: Pride heals slower than the problem. Ask for help early, admit mistakes, move on. Humility speeds everything up.
The next attempt is stronger. With experience and less fear, men often succeed the second or third time. Keep going.
